status: exploratory extension of the completed primary analysis; specified before running this extension
question: Does a folding-based filter preserve local graph connectivity more than an equally sized unstructured subset?
cohort: frozen 404 blocks, in-cell and cell-free target models, primary cutoff 0.5
pilot: first 24 block ids in frozen SHA-256 order; no outcome-based selection
uniform_null: uniform subsets independently within each full compatibility component, preserving the observed number of retained endpoints in each component
degree_null: same, additionally preserving retained endpoint counts within pooled-degree strata 0,1,2-3,4-7,8+ inside each component
statistic: E_F = 1 - sum(filtered component sizes squared) / sum(retained counts per original component squared)
degenerate_null: report exact invariance separately; a varied pairing or vertex subset is not sufficient to establish statistic variation
local_smoothness: mean squared retention difference across graph edges divided by within-component retention variance; label-permutation expectation computed analytically
uncertainty: Monte Carlo error conditional on graphs, and transcript-cluster bootstrap for mean contrasts; neither estimates organismal variability
interpretation: graph-conditioned model comparison, not an evolutionary selection test, experimental replication, or independent data validation
failure_criteria: null statistic invariant, no contrast against matched subsets, reversal under degree matching, or effect carried by a few dependent transcripts
